### A Snapshot of Global PV

### Markets

In 2024, global photovoltaic capacity rose to more than 2.2 TW *, up from 1.6 TW in 2023, with around 602 GW of new PV systems commissioned. This marks another record year for PV deployment, despite continued overcapacity in manufacturing and falling module prices that placed pressure on the entire value chain.

PV supplied more than 10% of global electricity consumption for the first time, cementing its position as a central pillar of the global energy transition.

#### Global Installations

2 246 GW were installed all over the world by the end of 2024

China is the world No. 1 PV market.

#### Market Trends

Utility-scale PV accounted for more than two-thirds of new capacity worldwide.

Residential and commercial prosumers continued to grow.

New applications such as floating PV on reservoirs, Agri-PV, and linear PV along transport corridors are showing strong potential and increased social acceptance.

China continues to dominate global PV manufacturing, in the context of oversupply and contributing to record-low prices.

#### Manufacturing and Trade

China continues to dominate global PV manufacturing, providing high efficiency and low cost modules

Brazil, Turkiye and South Africa have implemented import tariffs to protect local manufacturers.

India is scaling up local production through the Production Linked Incentive plan and import restrictions.

The EU is exploring resilience-based procurement and strategic subsidies under the Net-Zero Industry Act to support local value chains.

The USA is expanding domestic manufacturing under the Inflation Reduction Act, with over 40 GW per year of capacity.

Middle East countries, including Saudi Arabia and Oman, are developing integrated solar manufacturing hubs aimed at export oriented production.

Key Policy Instruments are being phased out across many markets as solar energy becomes increasingly cost competitive.

Feed-in tariffs remain common support mechanisms for prosumers, with details varying by region and maturity.

Net billing and net metering

are expanding as the preferred model for large-scale and commercial PV deployment.

Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs)

are being introduced for new buildings, especially within the EU and Asia-Pacific.

Mandatory rooftop solar requirements

are being created to support energy sharing among users.

Virtual self-consumption frameworks

are being developed in regions with high PV penetration, helping mitigate grid congestion and curtailment.

Storage incentive schemes

#### Challenges

Curtailment and Grid Congestion

As PV penetration grows, an increasing number of countries are facing challenges in managing variable generation. Curtailment due to demand mismatch and grid congestion, especially during midday peaks, is becoming more frequent.

Data Discrepancies

Global statistics are hampered by inconsistent reporting standards, including undocumented AC/DC conversion ratios, lack of data on recycled and repowered systems, off-grid installations, and decommissioned systems.

Manufacturing Imbalance

While China continues to dominate PV manufacturing, many local producers in other countries are struggling to compete. Even with new industrial policies and incentives, local supply chains in India, and the EU face ongoing cost and scale challenges.

Workforce and Skills Gaps

Rapid PV deployment has outpaced the availability of skilled labor in many countries. Workforce shortages affect project timelines, installation quality, and long term maintenance capacity, highlighting the need for training programs and education initiatives.

#### Future Outlook

Policy Evolution

National governments are increasingly aligning PV expansion with climate commitments, introducing reforms to support grid modernisation, energy storage, and local content requirements. Policy clarity and continuity remain essential.

Technology Integration

Stronger coupling of PV with energy storage systems, electric vehicles, and demand-side flexibility solutions is expected. Smart grid technologies will play a critical role in managing distributed generation.

Resilience and Localisation

Amid rising geopolitical and energy security concerns, countries are focusing on local PV manufacturing, skilled workforce development, and resilient supply chains, while also advancing circular economy and end-of-life strategies.

Sector Coupling and Innovation

PV is expected to play a larger role in decarbonising other sectors through power-to-X technologies, including green hydrogen production, electric heating, and electrified transportation.
